thread.title: 3 Best Stock Trading Apps From Top Online Brokers | Investor's Business Daily

author: APARNA NARAYANAN
title: 3 Best Stock Trading Apps From Top Online Brokers | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Looking for the best stock trading apps and mobile platforms? You might start with a look at the top-ranked firms in IBD's Best Online Brokers survey.
X Fidelity Investments, Charles Schwab ( SCHW ) and Interactive Brokers ( IBKR ) have been busy building out their offerings. They earned the highest ratings for Mobile Trading Platforms/Apps in IBD's survey.
Investors' preferences were identified in the survey of 2,762 people. As in previous years, IBD asked investors which brokerage features are most important to them and whether their primary broker did a good job in each of those categories.
So, what exactly have stock brokers done to enhance their mobile platforms? And how might their investment apps improve further?
Investor's Business Daily spoke to Fidelity, Schwab and Interactive Brokers to find out.
View The Full Best Online Brokers Special Report See Lists Of The Best Online Brokers Overall And In Every Category Interactive Brokers App Gets Overhaul, New Name In 2018, Interactive Brokers unleashed a raft of tools to make investing on the go more robust. The new and enhanced features include:
A brand-new web-based trading platform that works seamlessly across desktop and mobile A redesigned and renamed mobile trading platform Porting the Performance Profile tool to mobile Order presets that sync via the cloud, and more Interactive Brokers' new Client Portal is becoming the primary web trading platform. It's simpler to use than the venerable Trader Workstation, making it ideal for novice and occasional traders. It works on any device with a browser, be it desktop computer, tablet or smartphone. Client Portal allows customers to both manage accounts and trade equities in one place, making things simpler and faster, said Steve Sanders, Interactive Brokers' EVP of product development. Traditionally, the company separated web-based account management from its mobile trading app.
Interactive also gave its options and stock trading app a major refresh, renaming it IBKR Mobile. New tools, such as Option Exercise and Spread Template, cater to a client base of mostly active traders. The tools warn users if an option is out of the money and simplify creating multileg spreads, for example. The app now features two-factor authentication to boost account safety .
"We really wanted to make sure it's a powerful and feature-rich platform, while still being simple and easy to use and intuitive to navigate," Sanders said.
In the past year, Interactive ported popular trading tools from desktop to mobile platforms. One, called Performance Profile, shows the return-to-risk ratio of an option strategy, as well as profit probability and potential maximum return or maximum loss. Another, called Order Presets, now syncs a user's order presets and stock watchlists across all their devices, via the cloud.
Other improvements include picture-in-picture functionality for the in-app video player; a calendar showing key events tied to a client's stocks, such as earnings and dividend date; "persistent" trade buttons that make it easy to buy and sell no matter where you are in the app; and the addition of roughly 2,500 FAQs to Interactive's iBot tool, which allows investors to trade using voice commands.
In the next few weeks, Interactive Brokers plans to port its popular chart-trading tool, called Chart Trader, to its stock and options trading app.
Mobile trades accounted for 17.3% of overall trades at Interactive Brokers in the fourth quarter of 2018. Mobile trades grew 35% between 2016 and 2018.
Fidelity Investment Apps Offer P2P Payments Privately held Fidelity focused on improving the speed and stability of its mobile platform in the past year.
That doesn't mean the stock broker sat still on shiny new features for its investment app, one of the best in the business.
New in-app features introduced last year include:
A customizable start screen Detailed status tracking Contextual help on trade tickets Person-to-person payments Customers told Fidelity loud and clear that they wanted a customizable start screen. Many clients prefer to jump straight into their accounts or watchlists on opening the app, rather than see the standard news feed. Now they can choose what shows up on launching the app, said Scott Ignall, Fidelity's head of retail brokerage. They can customize the start screen, by dragging icons around, to organize tabs by importance.
Another new feature allows customers to view balances across all accounts, as well as all transaction requests, from one centralized location. The feature, called Universal Tracker, also offers step-by-step status tracking for more than 20 key transactions. Converting to a Roth IRA, setting up options trading , transferring assets — they're all in one handy place.
Meanwhile, trade-ticket help offers contextual icons to access information. Before placing a trade, customers can hit a question-mark icon next to "order type" to bring up a glossary, for example.
Last year, Fidelity made some key integrations for mobile users — PayPal ( PYPL ) for person-to-person (P2P) payments and Apple ( AAPL ) Messages Chat to get services help, among them.
According to Ignall, Fidelity has shifted away from developing its stock trading platform for web browsers first. Now mobile apps are the primary focus, and for good reason.
Mobile trades increased 32% over the past two years. They now account for 16.2% of overall brokerage trades, up from 14% a year ago. The Fidelity stock trading app saw a 36% increase in downloads over the past two years. Its millennial clients tend to trade on smartphones and tablets primarily.
"We want to make (mobile trading) as easy and as contextual as possible for our clients," Ignall said. "It's absolutely one of our critical investments and it will be for the future."
Schwab Stock Trading Apps Add Podcasts, Videos Charles Schwab focused last year on making the Schwab Mobile investment and trading app as snappy and responsive as possible.
In the past year, the online stock broker debuted or enhanced several features, including:
Customized media center Streamlined research experience Account aggregation Amazon Alexa support The Media Center section of Schwab's mobile app offers access to podcasts, YouTube video playlists, daily market updates and more. In 2018, Schwab added its popular Choiceology podcast to the offerings.
"It's really fun to see us experiment with things we typically haven't done a ton of, and it has been really well received by clients," said Kate O'Connor, vice president of digital platform at Charles Schwab.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The online broker also streamlined the investment research experience for investors on the move. So now, the most-used data points for making investment decisions are front and center when investors place a trade. For example, Today's Range and 52-Week High can more quickly and easily be seen on the redesigned Quote screen of the app. Schwab simplified other aspects of placing a trade. Type "QQQ" and the ticket automatically figures out you're trading an ETF, rather than making you choose what type of investment you're trying to trade.
"It puts the burden on us," O'Connor said. Schwab Equity Ratings — a data model that tries to identify which of 3,200 U.S. stocks will outperform or underperform — is now a centerpiece of in-app research, she added.
A redesigned landing page shows customers their full financial picture. It collects retirement, brokerage and banking accounts in one place, which Schwab calls account aggregation. Clients can even connect non-Schwab accounts to their dashboard. The app also depicts this aggregate view on a chart, showing progress in value of combined accounts on a day-to-day basis, over time.
Schwab tapped Amazon ( AMZN ) Alexa skills last year. Clients can use the Alexa-enabled Echo speaker to get stock quotes and market updates using their voice. Schwab plans to add support for Alphabet 's ( GOOGL ) Google Home this year. O'Connor called smart speakers "mobility oriented," describing voice- and touch-based applications as interconnected.
"We want our client to be able to access Schwab in whatever way they want, but we especially want them to be able to access it on the go," O'Connor said.
The number of Schwab Mobile app users increased 18% in 2018, as mobile trades vaulted more than 60% year over year. The app attracted close to 1 million unique users in December. In any given month, about 40% of mobile app users tend to exclusively use the app for investing, according to Schwab.
